premises: Al and Ti enrich in a surface oxide film on the HEA during high-temperature exposure
This oxide film is initially protective, preserving the fcc matrix and mechanical properties
Prolonged oxidizing exposure causes stress-induced defects (buckling, porosity) in the oxide, leading to spallation and inward oxygen diffusion
Reducing conditions prevent robust oxide formation, leading to a distinct degradation pathway (selective internal oxidation)
